cards.title: Microtasks run before the next task
cards.body: After each task, such as a timer or an event, the engine empties the whole microtask queue: promise callbacks and queueMicrotask. Only then does it render or take the next task. A loop of promises that never ends freezes the page like a while (true).

cards.title: A closure keeps the variable, not its value
cards.body: A function remembers the variables of the scope where it was made. If the variable changes later, the function sees the new value. let in a for loop makes a new binding for each turn, which is why it fixes the classic loop bug.

cards.title: Group an array without a reduce
cards.body: Object.groupBy (ES2024) returns an object with one array for each key. Map.groupBy does the same with a Map, for keys that are not strings.
cards.code:
const byTopic = Object.groupBy(cards, (card) => card.topic);
// { git: [...], http: [...] }

cards.title: forEach does not wait for an async callback
cards.body: items.forEach(async (item) => await save(item)) starts every save and returns at once; errors become unhandled rejections. Use for...of with await for one at a time, or await Promise.all(items.map(save)) to run them together.

cards.title: In which order does this log? setTimeout(() => log('a')); Promise.resolve().then(() => log('b')); log('c');
cards.body: The synchronous log runs first. The promise callback is a microtask and runs as soon as the current script ends. The timer is a task and runs after that.

cards.title: What is [] == false?
cards.body: Loose equality converts both sides to numbers: false is 0, and [] becomes '' then 0. Use === and the question never comes up.

cards.title: The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
cards.body: javascript.info covers the language from the basics to promises, generators and modules, with tasks at the end of each chapter.
